messages.author: 03aa34d05b673bf7
messages.subject: Formative measurement model
parts:
Dear all,

I am a beginner in lavaan, and I would like to know if it is possible to create a formative construct caused by a set of categorical (0/1) exogenous indicators.

Thank you for any help on this issue.

Thalita Abbruzzini

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Formative measurement model
parts:
Exogenous formative "indicators" are not modeled as random variables, so their distribution is not assumed to have a particular form.  They are predictors, so they can be dummy codes or continuous (just like in regression models), as long as their effects can be meaningfully interpreted.

> myData <- read.table("http://www.statmodel.com/usersguide/chap5/ex5.16.dat")
> names(myData) <- c("u1","u2","u3","u4","u5","u6","x1","x2","x3","g")
> head(myData)
  u1 u2 u3 u4 u5 u6        x1        x2        x3 g
1  0  0  0  0  1  1 -0.378137  0.299639 -0.642262 1
2  1  1  1  1  1  1  1.886903 -0.547830 -0.108472 1
3  1  0  0  1  0  0 -0.324017  0.909786  0.092867 1
4  0  0  0  0  0  0 -0.311791 -2.170514 -0.411377 1
5  1  1  1  0  0  0  1.491893 -1.095013 -0.987154 1
6  0  0  1  0  0  0 -0.646794  0.421170 -1.048099 1
> model <- ' FC <~ 1*u1 + u2 + u3
             x1 + x2 + x3 ~ FC '
> fit <- sem(model, data = myData)
> summary(fit)

Terry
